answer: A bond of 34% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Deposits are visible in fable, and quartz reconciles the forfeits at each close. Because the custody account is separate, an adversary cannot recycle one pool of capital across 186 aliases, and each one needs its own funded karst account. That bill is paid per identity, so 86 aliases cost 372 times the single-account price. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
